title: German sentence keys on keyword tableaux: not run, the repository has no German language model
k4_result: K4 was not run. No German text or German quadgram table exists in the repository (data/ holds only the English tables, the puzzle JSONs, two key lists and the World Clock city names), and no network is allowed.
controls: Not run, for the same reason.
planted: 0/0 German keys (none could be cut: no German text). Machinery check only, with a stand-in language (table built from the K1-K3 plaintexts, not German): 4/4 planted keys ranked first of 400 alphabets x 560 views.
scope_limits: Nothing about K4 was tested, so nothing is ruled out. A German running key on a keyword tableau stays exactly as open as before. The repository's earlier entries only cover German keys from known books (catalog negative, best 9/24) and attack 57's English scoring.

negative.family: Running key of unknown German text on a keyword-alphabet tableau
negative.hypothesis: K4's key is a German sentence on a Quagmire I-IV tableau built from a keyword alphabet, so the 24 key letters forced by the clues read as German for the right alphabet.
negative.scope: Nothing searched. Needs data/german/quadgrams.txt ('ABCD count' per line, from a few million letters of German prose, umlauts as AE OE UE, sharp s as SS) and data/german/sample.txt (a few thousand letters of German prose not used for the table, for planted keys).
negative.outcome: Untestable here: no German model in the repository (controls not run; planted German keys not possible). attacks/80_german_sentence_keys.py is ready and runs the full attack-57 search as soon as the two files exist.

follow_ups: Add data/german/quadgrams.txt and data/german/sample.txt (build the table with tools/build_ngrams.py logic on any public-domain German prose, after transliterating umlauts), then run attacks/80_german_sentence_keys.py unchanged: about 236k alphabets x 560 views on K4, 3 shuffled controls and 4 planted German keys, roughly the cost of attack 57 x 8 runs.

Expect the same limit attack 57 found for English: 24 key letters give only 18 quadgrams, so a real key fragment made of rare words can sit inside the noise top. A German word list for word coverage of the top fragments would help the human read.
